Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

# Green Party 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Overview
The manifesto addresses the cost of living crisis, climate change, and public service reform, presenting policy proposals across multiple sectors.

## Healthcare
The party proposes £28bn additional annual NHS funding by 2030, plus £20bn capital investment over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing GP access, ensuring NHS dentist availability (£3bn annually by 2030), boosting staff pay, and restoring public health budgets. They oppose NHS privatisation and support the NHS Reinstatement Bill. Mental health services would receive investment for 28-day therapy access, with counsellors in all schools.

## Social Care
Proposals include free personal care (similar to Scotland's model), £20bn annual investment, improved carer pay and career structures, and ending exploitation of overseas care workers.

## Housing
The party proposes 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering councils to introduce rent controls, ending no-fault evictions, and a £29bn five-year home insulation programme targeting EPC B standards.

## Energy
Plans include wind power providing 70% of electricity by 2030, no new fossil fuel licences, ending oil and gas subsidies, community energy ownership, and opposing new nuclear development. A carbon tax starting at £120/tonne, rising to £500/tonne, would be introduced.

## Economy
The manifesto proposes £40bn average annual green investment, bringing railways, water companies and major energy retailers into public ownership, a £15/hour minimum wage, maximum 10:1 pay ratios, and repealing anti-union legislation.

## Taxation
Proposals include a wealth tax (1% above £10m assets, 2% above £1bn), aligning capital gains with income tax rates, reforming inheritance tax, and a carbon tax estimated to raise £80bn annually by parliament's end.

## Welfare
Plans include £40/week Universal Credit increase, abolishing the two-child benefit cap, 5% disability benefit increase, ending the five-week benefit wait, and scrapping the bedroom tax.

## Environment
Proposals include a Rights of Nature Act giving legal personhood to nature, protecting 30% of land and seas by 2030, public water ownership, and Right to Roam legislation.

## Education
The party proposes £8bn school investment, £5bn for SEND provision, scrapping tuition fees, restoring maintenance grants, free school meals, and moving academies to local authority control.

## Transport
Plans include £10bn annual public transport subsidies, railway renationalisation, local bus control, £2.5bn annual cycling/walking investment, free bus travel for under-18s, ending petrol/diesel vehicle sales by 2027, and a frequent flyer levy.

## Democracy
Proposals include proportional representation, votes at 16, replacing the House of Lords with an elected chamber, and repealing the Elections Act 2022.

## Immigration
The party proposes ending the hostile environment policy, creating safe asylum routes, allowing asylum seekers to work during applications, and removing minimum income requirements for spousal visas.

## Foreign Policy
Positions include calling for an Israel-Gaza ceasefire, recognising Palestine, increasing overseas aid to 1% of GNI by 2033, working toward EU rejoining, and signing the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons while cancelling Trident.

## Funding
The manifesto estimates raising £50-70bn annually through tax reforms by parliament's end, with additional borrowing for capital investment. Total revenue spending would reach £161.6bn by 2030, with capital spending of £90.3bn.

# Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 Summary

The Liberal Democrats' 2024 manifesto outlines proposals across multiple policy areas under the banner of delivering a "fair deal" for citizens.

## Economy
The party proposes investing in renewable energy and home insulation to reduce energy bills and create jobs. They would replace business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy, support small businesses, invest in apprenticeships, and introduce Lifelong Skills Grants of £5,000 per adult. They commit to responsible fiscal management while seeking to improve trading relationships with Europe.

## Healthcare
Key proposals include guaranteeing GP appointments within seven days (24 hours for urgent cases), recruiting 8,000 additional GPs, ensuring NHS dentist access for urgent care, and placing mental health professionals in every school. They propose a guarantee for cancer treatment to begin within 62 days of referral and plan to address NHS staffing shortages.

## Social Care
The party proposes introducing free personal care based on the Scottish model, creating a Royal College of Care Workers, establishing a higher minimum wage for carers, and increasing support for unpaid carers including paid carer's leave and respite breaks.

## Education
Proposals include increasing school funding above inflation, recruiting specialist teachers, introducing tutoring guarantees for disadvantaged pupils, tripling the Early Years Pupil Premium, reinstating maintenance grants for students, and reforming Ofsted inspections.

## Housing
The manifesto commits to building 380,000 homes annually including 150,000 social homes, banning no-fault evictions, creating three-year default tenancies, establishing a national landlord register, and abolishing residential leaseholds.

## Environment
Environmental proposals include banning sewage discharges, transforming water companies into public benefit companies, targeting 90% renewable electricity by 2030, planting 60 million trees annually, and implementing a Clean Air Act. They aim for net zero emissions by 2045.

## Crime and Justice
The party proposes restoring community policing, guaranteeing police attendance at all burglaries, investing in court capacity to reduce backlogs, and creating an Online Crime Agency for digital offences.

## Immigration
They would abolish the current migration legislation, establish processing standards of three months for asylum claims, allow asylum seekers to work after three months, and create safe legal routes for refugees.

## Political Reform
Key reforms include introducing proportional representation for elections, giving 16-17 year-olds voting rights, capping political donations, enshrining the Ministerial Code in law, and reforming the House of Lords.

## Defence and International
The party commits to reversing Army cuts, maintaining NATO membership, spending at least 2.5% of GDP on defence, and supporting Ukraine. They propose a four-stage roadmap to improve EU relations, with eventual Single Market membership as a goal.
